criteria.text: The patient has enrolled onto EAY191 and has been given a treatment assignment to ComboMATCH to EAY191-N5 based on the presence of an actionable mutation as defined in EAY191
The patient has a HER2 amplified solid tumor except breast cancer.
If IHC is 0 or 1+, the patient is not eligible.
If IHC is 3+, the patient is eligible.
If IHC is 2+, ISH/FISH or NGS must be positive for the patient to be eligible.
The patient has recurrent or persistent disease.
The patient has no known evidence of RB1 loss or deletion including copy number loss or deleterious mutation.

The patient has disease that can be safely biopsied and agrees to a pre-treatment biopsy or, if disease cannot be safely biopsied, has archival tissue available from within 12 months prior to the date of registration on the ComboMATCH Registration Trial (EAY191).
The patient has measurable disease based on RECIST 1.1. A second measurable lesion outside of the biopsiable lesion is required.

Patients with treated brain metastases are eligible if follow up brain imaging after central nervous system (CNS) directed therapy shows no evidence of progression for 3 months or more and patient is not on steroids and is asymptomatic.
The patient has no known leptomeningeal disease.
The patient has received up to 5 prior lines of systemic therapy.
Prior therapy with trastuzumab or pertuzumab, either alone or in combination, antibody drug conjugates (ADC) such as DS8201a or T-DM1 is allowed.
The patient has no prior therapy with HER2 targeting tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) such as neratinib or tucatinib.
The patient has no prior therapy with CDK4/6 inhibition.

The patient has no cancer directed therapy within 3 weeks prior to registration. For oral therapy, the washout can be reduced to greater than or equal to 5 half lives of the drug. No HER2 targeting ADCs within 30 days prior to registration.
The patient is age ≥ 18.
The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of ≤ 2.
The patient is not pregnant and not nursing.
The patient has an Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 1,500 cells/mm^3.
The patient has Platelets ≥ 100,000 cells/mm^3.
The patient has Hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dl.
The patient has a Creatinine clearance (CrCL) of ≥ 30 mL/min by the Cockcroft-Gault formula.
The patient has a Total bilirubin level ≤ 1.5 x institutional upper limit of normal (ULN).
The patient has Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ≤ 3 x institutional upper limit of normal (ULN).

Patients with known history or current symptoms of cardiac disease, or history of treatment with cardiotoxic agents, should have a clinical risk assessment of cardiac function using the New York Heart Association Functional Classification. To be eligible for this trial, patients should be class 2B or better.
The patient has no active infection requiring parenteral antibiotics.

The patient has no current evidence of intra-abdominal abscess, abdominal/pelvic fistula (not diverted), gastrointestinal perforation, gastrointestinal (GI) obstruction, and/or need for drainage nasogastric or gastrostomy tube.

The patient has no current evidence of malabsorption or chronic diarrhea or any other significant gastro-intestinal disease (e.g gastrectomy, ileal bypass, Crohn's disease, gastroparesis), associated with moderate to severe diarrhea (grade 2 or more) or inability to tolerate oral therapy.
The patient has no lung disease causing dyspnea at rest.
The patient has no interstitial lung disease with ongoing signs and symptoms at the time of registration.
The patient has no history of allergic reaction to the study agents, compound of similar chemical or biologic composition of the study agents or any of their excipients.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "Testing the Use of Neratinib or the Combination of Neratinib and Palbociclib Targeted Treatment for HER2+ Solid Tumors (A ComboMATCH Treatment Trial)". Your earlier answers already covered 8 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you been enrolled in the EAY191 study and assigned to the ComboMATCH arm (EAY191-N5)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know what the EAY191 study is. I've only been on Tagrisso since the cancer spread.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: The trial asks about this: “The patient has a HER2 amplified solid tumor except breast cancer.”. Does this describe you?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if my tumor is HER2 amplified. The report just says HER2 negative, so I assume that means no.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, does your most recent pathology report state that your tumor is HER2 positive or HER2 negative?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: My report says HER2 negative.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you know if your most recent pathology report lists your HER2 status as IHC 0 or 1+?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know the specific IHC scores like 0 or 1+. My folder just says HER2 negative.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since the report says HER2 negative, do you know if it lists the score as IHC 0 or 1+? If you aren't sure, that's okay—just let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know the specific IHC scores like 0 or 1+. My folder just says HER2 negative.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since your report says HER2 negative, do you know if it lists the score as IHC 3+? If you aren't sure, that's okay—just let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if it lists the score as IHC 3+. My folder just says HER2 negative.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since your report says HER2 negative, do you know if it lists the score as IHC 2+? If you aren't sure, that's okay—just let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if it lists the score as IHC 2+. My folder just says HER2 negative.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, does your medical record show that the HER2 test was 'equivocal' or 'borderline' (often called IHC 2+), which would require a second test (like FISH or NGS) to confirm? If you aren't sure, that's okay—just let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if the test was equivocal or borderline. My folder just says HER2 negative.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if your medical records show any evidence of RB1 loss, deletion, or mutation? If you aren't sure, that's okay—just let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about RB1 loss or mutations. I'd have to dig out the full report to check for that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Would you be willing to have a biopsy before starting treatment, or do you have tissue samples from a previous biopsy within the last 12 months?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have tissue samples from my initial biopsy. I keep a folder of every report, so I should be able to get them.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if those tissue samples are from within the last 12 months? If not, would you be willing to have a new biopsy before starting treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know the exact date of that initial biopsy, but I have the folder with all the reports. I can check the date on them for you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever received treatment with trastuzumab or pertuzumab (brand names include Herceptin and Perjeta)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had trastuzumab or pertuzumab. I've only taken Tagrisso.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever taken neratinib or tucatinib (brand name Tukysa)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't taken neratinib or tucatinib. I've only taken Tagrisso.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever taken any CDK4/6 inhibitor medicines, such as palbociclib (Ibrance), ribociclib (Kisqali), or abemaciclib (Verzenio)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't taken any of those. I've only taken Tagrisso.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received any cancer treatment in the last 3 weeks?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any cancer treatment in the last 3 weeks. I just take my daily Tagrisso.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you 18 years of age or older?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I'm 58 years old.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any known heart conditions or symptoms, or have you ever received cancer treatments that might affect your heart?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No heart problems. I haven't had any treatments that would affect my heart.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have an active infection that requires antibiotics given by injection or IV?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any active infections right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any abdominal or pelvic infections, fistulas, blockages, or need a tube for drainage?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any abdominal or pelvic infections, fistulas, blockages, or need for drainage tubes.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any issues with nutrient absorption, chronic diarrhea, or other significant digestive conditions that make it hard to take pills by mouth?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any issues with nutrient absorption or chronic diarrhea. I'm able to take my daily Tagrisso pill just fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any lung disease that causes shortness of breath while resting?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have shortness of breath while resting. I still do the books and get around, though I tire out and can't do the heavy ranch work.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had an allergic reaction to neratinib, palbociclib, or any similar medications?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any allergic reactions to those medications. I've only taken Tagrisso so far.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
